_comment: This skill owns Layers 1-4: the milestone contract, ADRs, readiness, per-slice planning,
implementation and closeouts. Hard negatives are the three upstream skills, whose
vocabulary (vision, horizons, REQ-* baselines) overlaps most.

trigger.prompt: Produce the Layer 1 detailed planning, ADRs and readiness checklist for this milestone
Plan the first vertical slice: mini-spec, delivery stories and engineering tasks to a code-ready verdict
Implement the code-ready engineering tasks for this slice and keep it deployable
Write the slice closeout with acceptance verdicts and reproduce commands
This slice hit a contract gap — record a Step 4a handback instead of deciding it in code
Close out the milestone with its REQ-* evidence matrix and hand back to the roadmap
Add an ADR for a decision that affects more than one work package, with its rejected alternatives
Update ARCHITECTURE_OVERVIEW.md and TECH_STACK.md to match what actually shipped
Draft our durable product vision and North Star statement
Write a PR-FAQ and a Lean Canvas for this product idea
Sequence the remaining milestones on Now/Next/Later horizons by risk
Revalidate the remaining roadmap and promote the next milestone to Now
Write the REQ-* requirements baseline with EARS acceptance and NFRs

behavior.prompt: Run Steps 1-3 for milestone <slug>: spec-only, no product code.
expected_behavior: Reads INITIAL_REQUIREMENTS.md first and lifts scope, acceptance and REQ-* traceability into the plan
Promotes open questions into the pre-implementation checklist as gaps
Breaks the milestone into goals with acceptance criteria rather than coding instructions
Records whether ARCHITECTURE_OVERVIEW.md / TECH_STACK.md must be created or updated
Writes no product code and does not split the whole milestone into Layer 3-4
Runs the adversarial critique pass and ends with an explicit implementation-ready or not-ready verdict
Runs specs_check.sh and reports it error-free

behavior.prompt: Plan the next vertical slice for this milestone, then stop.
expected_behavior: Reads the Layer 1 contract and the previous slice's CLOSEOUT.md, not the previous slices' mini-specs
Plans this slice only, and does not pre-plan the remaining slices
Produces engineering tasks with objective done criteria, named tests, evidence-matrix rows and cited QA-* fitness functions
Keeps each artifact inside its size budget
Ends with an explicit code-ready or not-ready verdict and writes no product code

behavior.prompt: Implement slice 2. Engineering task ET-3 contradicts the frozen contract in the Layer 1 plan.
expected_behavior: Stops rather than deciding the contradiction in code
Records task-2/STEP_4A_HANDBACK.md with the contract citation, the question, options with consequences, and the owning authority
Sets the slice closeout status to implementation handback and does not mark the slice shipped
Makes no design, scope, contract or ADR decision, and invents no acceptance criteria
